source_name: European Payments Initiative / Wero and EuroPA alliance communications
why_relevant: Determines the medium-term fate of Flik: Slovenian banks are weighing a Wero (centralising) path against EuroPA (interlinking national schemes), and the Flik scheme committee is reportedly preparing documentation on a EuroPA link-up. Membership announcements from EPI/EuroPA would be the first hard signal of a Slovenian rail change. Note: as of this pass Slovenia/Flik is reported NOT to be an official EuroPA member.

source_name: Open Banking Tracker — Slovenia country page
why_relevant: Third-party aggregator enumerating Slovenian ASPSPs, their API portals and licensed TPPs. Useful as a snowball index to discover bank developer portals and fintechs we would otherwise miss; figures should be verified against BSI/EBA registers rather than trusted directly.

source_name: denar.svetidej.com — Slovenian fintech services directory (Open Banking, mBills entries)
why_relevant: Local-language consumer directory of Slovenian fintech services and open-banking explainers; valuable purely as an actor-discovery index for smaller wallet/A2A players and for local terminology, not as an evidence source.

source_name: Banka Slovenije — Letno poročilo (Annual Report) and fee/cost comparison analyses
source_subtype: central bank annual report and fee surveys
why_relevant: The BSI annual report contains a payment-systems chapter (BIPS/TIPS oversight, instant payments migration, IPR implementation) with volume and value figures for the domestic instant system. Its recurring 'Primerjava stroškov nekaterih bančnih storitev' and 'Analiza nadomestil' publications price instant transfers, Flik and card payments — the pricing lever that drives substitution away from cash and cards.

source_name: ATMinfo.si - Stanje bankomatske mreze v Sloveniji
source_subtype: independent monitoring site / ATM estate tracker
why_relevant: Independent near-real-time monitor of the Slovenian ATM estate: live count of ATMs (approx 1,046 observed), per-bank availability/uptime percentages for eight banks (NLB, NKBM/OTP, SKB, UniCredit, Addiko, Sparkasse, Delavska hranilnica, DBS), an interactive ATM map, a searchable ATM list, historical graphs and an alarm feed. It self-declares that its data is sourced from openbanking.bankart.si, i.e. it is effectively a rendered front-end over the national PSD2 ATM-location API. This is the single richest machine-observable view of ATM estate size, per-operator share and geographic coverage for cell 10, and because it is timestamped and refreshed it allows longitudinal tracking of closures rather than only annual snapshots.

source_name: Banka Slovenije - Gotovina (cash section: banknotes and coins, cash supply, counterfeits)
source_subtype: central bank cash operations pages and annual report
why_relevant: Banka Slovenije organises the supply of banknotes and coins to Slovenia and decides on issuance and withdrawal from circulation. This section carries cash-in-circulation figures, cash supply arrangements, and counterfeit statistics - the demand-side counterpart to the ATM estate. Cumulative net cash issued (reported at 5.61 billion euro from euro adoption to end-2017 in the annual report) and counterfeit withdrawal counts give an independent read on cash usage intensity that is not derivable from card statistics. The central bank's cash department is also the counterparty that accredits cash handlers and recyclers under the Article 6 framework.

source_name: Predlog Zakona o dostopnosti in uporabi placilnih sredstev (ZDUPS) - eUprava e-demokracija public consultation
why_relevant: The single most consequential live regulatory event for this cell. The Ministry of Finance published the draft ZDUPS on 17 July 2026 (government act ref 2026-1611-0063), public consultation closed 17 August 2026. It was prepared with Banka Slovenije to implement the new Article 74a of the Constitution guaranteeing the right to use cash. Substantively it would oblige credit institutions and Posta Slovenije to maintain a cash-point network with prescribed geographic coverage: an ATM within 5 km of the centre of settlements over 1,000 inhabitants, a branch near settlements over 3,000, a transitional target that by 31 December 2029 at least 90 percent of the population has cash access within 5 km by road, plus a free basic payment package including at least five free out-of-network ATM withdrawals per month. Draft texts and impact assessments in such consultations routinely contain otherwise unpublished coverage statistics and gap maps.

source_name: Ministrstvo za finance RS (gov.si) - payments and cash accessibility policy
why_relevant: Sponsoring ministry for ZDUPS and the publisher of the press releases, consultation summaries and post-consultation statements about how many responses were received and which provisions will change. The ministry has already stated publicly that it reviewed the consultation responses in consultation with Banka Slovenije. Ministry communications are where the political framing of the branch/ATM closure debate is set and where the government's own count of cash-access gaps is likely to be first disclosed.

source_name: Euronet EFT Slovenija - independent ATM deployer (Slovenian site)
why_relevant: Euronet is the principal independent (non-bank) ATM deployer in Slovenia and globally operates roughly 55,000 ATMs across 60+ countries. Its Slovenian commercial site is segmented exactly along this cell's fault lines: a banks/outsourcing page, an explicit 'Bankomati za obcine' (ATMs for municipalities) page targeting the access-to-cash gap left by bank withdrawals, mobile ATMs for events, and internal/off-premise ATMs. The municipalities page is the direct commercial counterpart of the closure debate - it evidences who fills the gaps and on what terms. Euronet is also central to the surcharge controversy (free withdrawals for domestic cardholders ended in February, per press reporting).

source_name: OPSI - Evidenca imetnikov licenc po Zakonu o zasebnem varovanju (register of private security licence holders)
source_subtype: national open data portal dataset / statutory register
why_relevant: The definitive machine-readable census of Slovenian CIT operators. The Ministry of the Interior issues and revokes private security licences, and this open-data record contains company name, registered office, business registration number (maticna stevilka), activity code, licence number and TYPE, recorded legal violations, and issuance/revocation dates with current status. Because 'prevoz in varovanje gotovine ter drugih vrednostnih posiljk' is a distinct licence type, the dataset can be filtered to yield the complete legal population of cash-in-transit firms in Slovenia, with entry and exit dates - i.e. structural market data on the CIT segment that no commercial report provides.

source_name: SPOT / eVEM - Prevoz in varovanje gotovine ter drugih vrednostnih posiljk (regulated activity and licence pages)
why_relevant: The authoritative definition of the CIT activity and its licence conditions, and the entry point that names the competent authority (Ministry of the Interior), the licence certificate, and the legal prerequisites (a permanently employed security manager, trained personnel, specially adapted vehicles). It anchors the correct legal terminology for every downstream search and points onward to the licence register, the governing act and the implementing rulebook. Essential for building the cell's glossary correctly rather than searching on colloquial terms.

source_name: Zbornica za razvoj slovenskega zasebnega varovanja (ZRSZV) - private security chamber
why_relevant: The sector chamber for private security, which runs the statutory further-training programme specifically for cash transport and valuables guarding (izpopolnjevanje za prevoz in varovanje gotovine). Training-programme enrolment, member lists and chamber position papers are an indirect but reliable read on CIT sector size, labour supply and consolidation. Chambers also lobby on rulebook amendments, so their publications surface cost complaints and volume claims from CIT operators that are otherwise unpublished.

source_name: Slovenian CIT operator corporate sites (Sintal, G4S Slovenija, Varnost Vic, FIT varovanje, IBS Varovanje)
why_relevant: The named actor set for the cash logistics leg of this cell. Sintal describes armed, uniformed CIT crews, satellite vehicle tracking from its monitoring centres, and a cash-degradation system triggered on robbery; G4S Slovenija markets cash transport with anti-robbery escort; Varnost Vic, FIT varovanje and IBS Varovanje all list prevoz gotovine/prevoz denarja among their service lines. Their service pages reveal capability scope (vault services, ATM replenishment, cash processing/recycling) and their client references occasionally identify which banks outsource ATM cash handling - a fact rarely published by the banks themselves.

source_name: Zdruzenje mestnih obcin Slovenije (ZMOS) - ZDUPS coverage and municipal position
why_relevant: Municipalities are the aggrieved party in the ATM closure debate and ZMOS is their organised channel into the legislative process. It has published dedicated pages tracking ZDUPS at two separate stages (March 2026 and July 2026), which means it maintains a running institutional record of the bill and of municipal objections. Municipal associations collect member reports of specific closures - place-level detail that never reaches central bank aggregates. The parallel association SOS (Skupnost obcin Slovenije) should be tracked alongside it.

source_name: Municipal ATM subsidy decisions and council minutes (e.g. Obcina Logatec)
source_subtype: municipal official gazettes, council minutes, budgets, procurement notices
why_relevant: Where a bank withdraws, some Slovenian municipalities pay to keep an ATM running - reporting indicates Logatec has six ATMs of which the municipality subsidises two, including retaining the ATM in upper Logatec through subsidy. Municipal budgets, council agendas and public procurement notices for such subsidies disclose the actual per-ATM annual cost of rural cash access, a number banks and deployers otherwise treat as commercially confidential. Aggregating these across municipalities yields a bottom-up cost curve for the access-to-cash obligation now being legislated.

source_name: Posta Slovenije - denarne storitve (postal cash access network)
source_subtype: state-owned postal operator service pages and annual reports
why_relevant: Posta Slovenije is being written into ZDUPS as a counted node in the national cash-point network, and it already functions as a de facto cash access channel: it offers cash withdrawal over POS terminals to holders of Visa, Maestro, Mastercard, Diners, Discover and Karanta cards, including non-customers of the partner bank. Its treatment of every card transaction on its POS as a cash withdrawal has itself been a public controversy. Post office counts and closures are therefore a second, parallel cash-access estate that must be tracked alongside ATMs - and postal network rationalisation is the same rural-retreat story as bank branch closure.

source_name: Bank ATM and branch locator pages (NLB, OTP banka, UniCredit Bank Slovenija, Delavska hranilnica, SKB, Addiko, Sparkasse, DBS)
why_relevant: Each bank publishes its own branch and ATM locator, which is the primary-source ground truth for that operator's estate and the raw material behind PSD2 aggregation. Diffing locator contents over time detects individual site closures at address level before any aggregate statistic reflects them, and the per-bank split lets you attribute the national decline to specific institutions. Delavska hranilnica and UniCredit locators were both surfaced in local-language search; ATMinfo's per-bank table confirms the eight-bank universe.

source_name: OZS - Obrtno-podjetniska zbornica Slovenije (Chamber of Craft and Small Business) - ZDUPS consultation response
why_relevant: The small-business chamber is the merchant-side stakeholder in the cash debate: its members both accept cash (and therefore need deposit access and CIT services) and would be obliged under ZDUPS to accept at least one electronic payment method. Its consultation commentary and zastopanje (advocacy) pages capture merchant complaints about cash deposit costs, branch closures affecting daily takings, and card acceptance costs - the merchant-facing half of the cash-access ecosystem that bank-side sources omit.

source_name: OPSI - Odprti podatki Slovenije (national open data portal), Banka Slovenije publisher view
why_relevant: The national open data portal is the aggregator that exposes which public bodies publish machine-readable datasets relevant to this cell. It already surfaced two directly relevant registers (private security licence holders, list of licence holders) and provides a filtered view of Banka Slovenije datasets. As a pointer it should be swept systematically for datasets on settlements and population (needed to compute the 5 km / 1,000-inhabitant coverage tests in ZDUPS), municipal boundaries, and any cash-access geography published by ministries.

source_name: Academic and student theses on cash transport and ATM security in Slovenia (e.g. academia.si diploma on comparison of cash transport and protection)
why_relevant: Slovenian diploma and masters theses on private security routinely compare CIT providers, describe operational practice, and reproduce operator-supplied data (fleet sizes, route economics, ATM servicing frequency) that companies will not disclose to a researcher directly. They also cite the regulatory framework precisely. Combined with the national repository, this is an underrated route to CIT operational detail. The national aggregator repozitorij.uni-lj.si / dKUM and the Univerza v Mariboru Faculty of Criminal Justice output should be swept alongside this single example.
